stem: A nonpregnant adult has right-upper-quadrant pain and suspected biliary disease without fever or leukocytosis. Which initial imaging test is rated 'Usually Appropriate' by the ACR?
rationale: ACR Appropriateness Criteria for right-upper-quadrant pain rate abdominal ultrasound as Usually Appropriate for initial imaging in the relevant suspected biliary-disease scenario.
educational_objective: Identify ultrasound as the usual initial imaging study for suspected biliary disease in right-upper-quadrant pain.
source_document_title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria — Right Upper Quadrant Pain
source_locator: Variant 2: suspected biliary disease without fever or high WBC; US abdomen — Usually Appropriate
source_claim_supported: Abdominal ultrasound is a Usually Appropriate initial imaging study for suspected biliary disease in the specified RUQ-pain scenario.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13/PDF p.17
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — diagnostic imaging
correction_summary: Corrected the source-name/URL mismatch and anchored the answer to the ACR's exact Variant 2 appropriateness rating.
